lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project milkworts through their unusual zygomorphic flower: 5 sepals with 2 enlarged petaloid wing sepals, 3–5 true petals including a keel, usually 8 stamens, and a superior usually 2-locular ovary; then reconcile the recent Polygala→Senega/Rhinotropis splits.

project_scope.selection_mode: Source pool across Polygala, Rhinotropis and Senega; current teaching genera collapse to Rhinotropis + Senega.
project_scope.note: Four source rows represent three species-level concepts plus one accepted variety nested within Rhinotropis lindheimeri. Source Polygala alba is now Senega alba; source Polygala lindheimeri var. lindheimeri belongs under Rhinotropis lindheimeri var. lindheimeri.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look at one flower from the side. Find 5 sepals, but notice that the inner lateral pair are enlarged and petal-like ('wings'). Then find the true lower petal forming a keel around the stamens and style.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Project plants are herbs to subshrubs with simple exstipulate leaves, usually alternate but arrangement can vary in the family. Leaves alone are not a safe family ID.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and strongly zygomorphic. Calyx usually 5-merous with 3 smaller outer sepals and 2 enlarged inner wing sepals. Corolla commonly 3 petals in the project Senega-type architecture, with a lower keel often crested; Rhinotropis commonly has a beaked keel. Stamens commonly 8 with filaments united into a sheath/column. Ovary superior, usually 2-locular with one ovule per locule.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a flattened 2-locular dehiscent capsule in the project concepts, typically with one seed per locule; seeds are commonly pubescent and arillate.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: The fastest family door is 'petal-looking sepals + true keel petal + united stamens.' Then use keel crest versus beak and habit to route to current genus.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: flower face → wing sepals vs petals → keel → staminal sheath → superior ovary/capsule → Senega vs Rhinotropis → current-name card
visual_lesson.intro: Milkworts are perfect for visual anatomy because the flower looks pea-like at first glance, but the parts are not equivalent. The big 'wings' are sepals, not petals.

steps.title: 1 · Prove the wings are sepals
steps.photo_role: flower front/side macro with colored overlays
steps.look_for: Two large lateral petaloid structures outside the true corolla; label them as inner sepals (wings), with the 3 smaller outer sepals also shown.
steps.why_it_matters: This prevents the most intuitive but incorrect read of a Polygalaceae flower.

steps.title: 2 · Find the true keel petal
steps.look_for: The lower median corolla petal folded into a keel around the reproductive column; in Senega-type project taxa the keel is crested, while Rhinotropis has a beaked/snouted keel.
steps.why_it_matters: Keel architecture is the easiest current-genus teaching split in this pool.

steps.title: 3 · Expose the staminal sheath
steps.look_for: Usually 8 stamens with filaments joined basally into a trough-like sheath around the style.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms Polygalaceae reproductive architecture rather than relying on flower color.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the flower to the capsule
steps.look_for: A superior usually 2-locular ovary maturing into a flattened capsule, commonly with one seed in each locule.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds a fruit confirmation and ties the flower to the family plan.

steps.title: 5 · Senega door
steps.look_for: Former broad-Polygala project species with a lobed/fimbriate keel crest rather than the unlobed beak of Rhinotropis; S. alba is white-flowered while S. lutea has bright yellow-orange capitate racemes.
steps.why_it_matters: Turns the recent generic split into a visible flower-architecture lesson rather than a memorization problem.

steps.title: 6 · Rhinotropis door
steps.look_for: A distinct beaked or snout-like keel with an unlobed projection; project taxon is a dryland perennial/subshrub.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA specifically keys Rhinotropis by the beaked keel and related sepal/fruit characters.

steps.title: 7 · Teach the recent name changes
steps.look_for: Polygala alba → Senega alba; Polygala lindheimeri → Rhinotropis lindheimeri; source var. lindheimeri → Rhinotropis lindheimeri var. lindheimeri.
steps.why_it_matters: Keeps older Texas floras, FNA-era names and the current Kew backbone connected without duplicate learner concepts.

comparisons.title: Polygalaceae vs Fabaceae
comparisons.rule: Both may look 'pea-flowered,' but the structures differ. In Polygalaceae the large lateral wings are sepals and the lower keel is a petal; Fabaceae papilionoid flowers use banner, wings and keel as petals. Polygalaceae also commonly has an 8-stamen sheath and a 2-locular capsule rather than a one-carpel legume.

comparisons.title: Senega vs Rhinotropis
comparisons.rule: Project Senega concepts retain the traditional crested-keel milkwort architecture; Rhinotropis is characterized by a beaked/snouted keel with an unlobed projection and often a dryland subshrub habit.

visual_lesson.caveat: Modern generic limits changed recently. Flora of North America (2021) still describes Senega alba and S. lutea under Polygala, while the current Kew 2026 backbone accepts Senega. Use the older descriptions for morphology but current names for canonical taxonomy.

genera.fast_cue: crested-keel milkwort; project concepts include white S. alba and orange-yellow S. lutea
